articles.title: Emma Raducanu: Briton deserves celebration not cynicism after Wimbledon withdrawal, says Jonathan Overend
articles.summary: Emma Raducanu was forced to pull out of Wimbledon with a stress fracture but did her run to the Queen's Club final affect her physical condition? Watch the ATP and WTA Tours live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, streaming service NOW and the Sky Sports app
articles.body:
Did Emma Raducanu's run to the Queen's Club final break her? Jonathan Overend examines what went wrong for the British No 1 on the eve of Wimbledon.

Raducanu withdrew from Wimbledon on Sunday because of a stress fracture in her right leg, leaving the tournament without its highest-profile British player.

Raducanu announced the decision on Instagram on Sunday evening. She had been set to open play on No 1 Court on Monday against Antonia Ruzic.

  • Not got Sky? Get Sky Sports or stream with no contract

The 23-year-old had been dealing with the injury since a run to the final at Queen's Club this month, but said earlier on Sunday at a news conference that she still hoped to play at the All England Club.

"It can't be overstated how difficult it is for these British players to pull out of Wimbledon the day before it starts and I think so much of the talk around Raducanu is about the frequency of the injuries and how fragile she appears to be," said Sky Sports' lead tennis commentator, Jonathan Overend.

"Let's forget about that for a moment and think of a human being who was about to play in a tournament that she's had some really good results in the past - off the back of reaching the final at Queen's with her hopes presumably pretty high for a decent run here as a seeded player.

"To have to pull out the night before it starts, I just hope the levels of cynicism are just tempered a little bit.

"There's no way she would have wanted this situation, which is why she left it as long as she did because she wanted to give herself every chance of playing.

"It's devastating for her, disappointing for the tournament, but I hope everybody wishes her a speedy recovery because she's been so unlucky with injuries."

'Stress fracture hasn't just happened overnight'

Raducanu has not won a tour-level tournament before or after her surprising run to the US Open title as a qualifier at the age of 18. But she impressed at Queen's Club with some of her best tennis since that triumph, before losing to Donna Vekic in the final.

She said on Sunday that she first felt her injury during the clay-court season before it was aggravated at the grass-court warm-up event.

"Talking to people who have experience of stress fractures the general feeling is that this doesn't happen suddenly, so it's something that she's known about and has been managing, or it's something that has been affecting her, but she hasn't known about it. It hasn't just happened overnight," said Overend.

"The tennis tour is so arduous and so rigorous, there's no time to breathe, but it's no great surprise she should play through that week at Queen's, then have a practice week where suddenly pain has emerged.

"This disruption has clearly affected her practice this week here at Wimbledon even though she's tried to keep her spirits up. She's been photographed smiling, she's been curtailing some sessions and she's been spotted leaving the courts with protection around the shin.

"This is obviously something that they've been managing this week at the very least and quite possibly for the weeks before it as well. It makes her run to the Queen's final all the more remarkable and that should be celebrated.

"She's tried and tried and tried to make the start line here and it just hasn't happened."

'Raducanu is doing something right'

Raducanu is wiser and crucially back with old coach Andrew Richardson - the coach she split ‌with shortly after her US Open triumph.

She showed signs of rediscovering her spark and returning to the free-flowing tennis she was known for. That was evident at Queen's with her run securing a seeding of 30 at Wimbledon before her withdrawal.

"That is an incredible achievement when you consider the quantity of players who are out there and the depth of the talent," Overend explained. "To get to that ranking, she must be doing something right.

"There is a presumption that she should be higher and that presumption is around the fact that she won the US Open in 2021, therefore she should be a much better player than 30 in the world. I would disagree!

"If you asked me what is Raducanu's base level, I would say it's somewhere between 20 and 30. That to me is a really good level to be at.

"To the general public, seeded 27 or 28 is nowhere, but to those of us in the game you know how hard you have to work to get to that sort of level, so is she doing that badly? No! She's actually doing pretty well to maintain that ranking, but the key point, does she need a long period injury free of stability in her career? Absolutely! And just when we thought we were going to get it this summer, she's hit by another setback."

Overend added that the reunion with coach Richardson has already proved to be a success.

"There were signs of good improvement to her game [at Queen's] and if she can have some stability then I hope she sees the benefit of having a long-term coach that ultimately helped her to her biggest career achievement."

articles.title: Arthur Fery: British No 1 heads into American hard-court swing with areas he can improve ahead of US Open, according to Tim Henman
articles.summary: Tim Henman looks ahead to what's to come for new British No 1 Arthur Fery as the 24-year-old from Wimbledon prepares for the US Open; watch the ATP, WTA Tours and US Open from Aug 30 live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, streaming service NOW and the Sky Sports app
articles.body:
British No 1 Arthur Fery will head into the American hard-court swing with areas he can improve ahead of the US Open - but that's "exciting", says Tim Henman.

The wild card's surprise run to the Wimbledon semi-finals has injected a much-needed shot of positivity and given British fans a new name to follow in the Grand Slams - starting at the US Open in New York - live on Sky Sports Tennis from August 30.

The challenge for the 24-year-old now is to acclimatise to his new standing in the game and the loss of anonymity and the freedom that brings with it.

  • Latest tennis score updates and results 🎾
  • Download Sky Sports app for analysis, news and video 📺
  • Not got Sky? Get Sky Sports or stream with no contract 📱

The 23-year-old, who has soared to 36 in the world from No 114, was the last player standing in what was an otherwise dismal tournament for the host nation, but he became only the fifth British man this century to reach the second week at the All England Club.

Fery has earned direct entry to a Masters event for the first time in Cincinnati - 13-23 August - before appearing at the Winston-Salem Open from 23-29 August ahead of his debut at Flushing Meadows.

Speaking at Royal Birkdale ahead of The Open, Henman called Fery's dream run at the All England Club "amazing" and "transformational for his career and his life".

The former British No 1 said: "He started the year at 185 in the world, qualified in Melbourne and then has continued to improve his ranking - then getting a wild card at Wimbledon ranked 114 and winning five matches getting to the semi-finals it was an incredible performance - and I think it also shows the fine margins between these top players.

"If you're in the top 250 in the world you're an extremely good player and on your day you've got a chance of beating anyone, so huge for him to be 36 in the world now getting to the other Grand Slams and Masters 1000, so he's got an opportunity to really plan his schedule moving forward."

With July 20 rankings being used for the US Open main draw, it means Fery has no time to improve his current ranking of No 36, but a few withdrawals could help him nudge into a seeding position, which would be a massive boost.

"I mean it's interesting that actually the ranking points will come on after Wimbledon and then the entries are six weeks out so I think the first tournament he will take advantage of that is Cincinnati," explained Henman.

The 2004 US Open semi-finalist also believes Fery will only improve his overall power in order to compete with top-tier opponents.

"He's still got a lot of areas that he can improve in his game and I think that's exciting when you know you're young," said Henman. "I can't wait to watch him we need those British players at the top of the game and yeah he's got a great opportunity.

"We needed that because those first couple of days were pretty rough for British tennis, but it was brilliant to see Arthur play so well and if Emma [Raducanu] and Jack [Draper] can be back fit, then there's also Katie Boulter, Cam Norrie, while Jan Choinski has just broken into the top 100 - he's 75 in the world now - so you want those British players creating stories at the biggest events."

Fery ready for 'attention' like Raducanu after Wimbledon run

Fery admits he might be plunged into the media spotlight in a similar manner to Raducanu following his fairy tale run at Wimbledon.

"Yes, even already a little bit during the tournament I was thinking of life after and how I was going to handle all that because we've seen it with people who've broken through in that manner before," Fery told Sky News' Jacquie Beltrao.

"With Emma obviously, Emma won a Slam and I didn't but there was still a lot of media attention.

"It is going to be really important to handle that - the expectation from myself and also the public."

The Brit is ready for more time in the media glare as he competes against the top players in tennis.

"It means I can play the top players week in week out and compare myself to them and keep working on my tennis," said Fery.

"I am going to have to get accustomed to the full life of tour with more media attention and all of that but I think I'm ready for it.

"It is going to be a first as well playing the US Open. I didn't even play qualifiers last year so it's going be a great experience."

He is also relaxed about the possibility of being among the top-32 seeded players for Flushing Meadows.

"I might already be in there [the top 32] if I'm lucky, a few withdrawals," said Fery.

"I don't think I will be able to contribute to the ranking anymore before the list comes out for the US Open, because it's going to come out soon.

"Being seeded obviously protects you a little bit from the top guys, but it's my first main draw that I qualify for directly with my ranking so just going to take it as it goes."

articles.title: Emma Raducanu: British No 1 could end her season after US Open withdrawal with stress fracture
articles.summary: Emma Raducanu will skip the US Open due to a stress fracture, and Annabel Croft says Brit could forego the rest of the season;watch the ATP and WTA Tours and US Open from August 30 live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, streaming service NOW and the Sky Sports app
articles.body:
Emma Raducanu could benefit from ending her season early to focus on recovery and secure a protected ranking before making her return in 2027, according to former British No 1 Annabel Croft.

The 23-year-old suffered a stress fracture to her right lower leg during the grass-court season and made a late decision to pull out of Wimbledon.

And following consultation with her medical team, Raducanu on Monday concluded she will be unable to play at the US Open later this month - live on Sky Sports.

  • Latest tennis scores and results 🎾
  • Download Sky Sports app for analysis, news and video 📺
  • Not got Sky? Get Sky Sports or stream with no contract 📱

Raducanu has only recently taken her first tentative steps back on court while wearing a protective boot, and the latest setback is another blow for the Brit after a frustrating 12 months plagued by persistent physical issues.

Speaking on Sky Sports Tennis, former player-turned-TV analyst Croft admitted "she's been unbelievably unlucky with injury problems."

"There are so many injuries out there but it seems like she never gets a clear run where she's able to really go for it with her tennis and her body and her mind and everything injury free and just keep the momentum going."

After a foot injury severely hampered her pre-season training, Raducanu then spent two-and-a-half months off court with a post-viral illness after initially falling unwell in early February.

She finally returned for the end of the clay-court season having rehired Andrew Richardson, the coach who guided her to the US Open title, but the pair's time on court together has been limited.

Raducanu enjoyed one of the best weeks of her career by reaching her biggest final since New York at Queen's Club in June but it was that effort that triggered her latest setback.

She was not among the players named in Great Britain's team for the Billie Jean King Cup Finals in late September.

"I've seen lots of pictures of her posting with the boot on her leg and just trying to serve, to keep her racket going and showing everybody that she's doing everything she can. But clearly, it's not healed up," said Croft, who retired from the professional tour at the age of 21.

A protected ranking for Raducanu?

There will now be question marks over whether Raducanu, who will slide from her current ranking of 49, will compete again in 2026 with the temptation of a protected ranking.

Should she miss at least six months of competition due to injury, she can use a special ranking for a select number of events upon her return. This would be her top-50 ranking from during the grass season - the last time she competed and received prize money for a tournament.

Raducanu is at the risk of dropping down the rankings with a lot of points to defend following last year's north American hard-court swing in Washington, Canada, Cincinnati, and the US Open.

"It wouldn't be a surprise if she made that decision [close down her season]," said Croft, a former world No 24. "That wouldn't be such a bad decision to take because you can fully heal, rest up, get as much treatment as possible and then come out fully fit, raring to go at the start of next year.

"Maybe if there's a worry about the ranking drop with so many points to defend and potentially that ranking could plummet, although she might benefit from the protected ranking.

"All of these factors have to be considered, don't they? But at the end of the day, your health is your wealth, as they say, and that is the most important factor and she just needs to get herself fit.

"It's an unusual injury. I mean, I've had calf muscle injuries, which were not nice at all. And the minute you push off, you tweak it and it feels tight but the one thing that I've always thought about Raducanu, particularly when we saw her at Queen's Club on the grass where she played such beautiful tennis, is that she's very light on her feet. Movement has always been one of her strengths.

"She's such a great athlete. She moves around the ball. She's light on her feet and gets into great positions where she never looks off balance. But movement will be part of a major strength of what she brings out onto the court. That needs to be absolutely 100 per cent."

Previous winners of the US Open

In the Open era, Roger Federer, Pete Sampras and Jimmy Connors are tied with the most men's singles titles, with five.

Novak Djokovic will be hoping to get to that number this year; he is tied on four with Rafael Nadal and John McEnroe as he continues to chase a record-breaking 25th Grand Slam title.

Serena Williams and Chris Evert share the record for women's titles with six, ahead of Steffi Graf (five) and Martina Navratilova (four).

Carlos Alcaraz and Aryna Sabalenka are the respective reigning champions, though Emma Raducanu, Jannik Sinner, Iga Swiatek and Coco Gauff are also recent winners.

Alcaraz will both show up to the US Open without having played in Canada or Cincinnati with Sinner pulling out injured.

Since the beginning of the Masters format in 1990, no man has ever won the US Open without playing at least one of these two events.

Is Emma Raducanu playing?

No! The British No 1 will miss the Grand Slam because of the stress fracture in her right leg that she sustained during the grass-court season and forced her to pull out of Wimbledon.

It has been a frustrating 12 months for Raducanu with more persistent physical issues.

Will Jack Draper be fit?

The 2024 semi-finalist will miss this year's tournament as he continues to recover from bone bruising in his left arm.

The injury has been a blow for the 24-year-old, who has managed only a handful of tournaments since first stepping away from the tour a year ago with the same issue.

There will still be a strong British contingent in qualifying. In men's singles qualifying, stars of the summer Jacob Fearnley, Jack Pinnington Jones, Toby Samuel and Billy Harris are set to feature.

Meanwhile, on the women's side, Fran Jones - who recently won back-to-back WTA 125 titles - is a player to watch, with Dart, Katie Swan, Heather Watson and Jodie Burrage also in contention.

Qualifying starts from Monday 24 August.

Cameron Norrie will feature in the main draw at Flushing Meadows along with Britain's newest star Arthur Fery for the first time in his career after his remarkable run to the Wimbledon semi-finals as a wild card which has seen his ranking soar.

A hat-trick for Sabalenka?

World No 1 Sabalenka will look to become the first woman to win three straight US Open titles since Serena Williams from 2012-14.

US Open boosts prize money to record-setting level

The US Open has announced another bumper increase in prize money for this month's tournament.

An overall prize fund of 108 million US dollars (approximately £80 million) is the biggest in the sport's history and represents a 20 per cent rise for the second consecutive year.

The winners of the singles trophies will each receive 5.5million dollars (approximately £4 million), while first-round prize money has been ramped up to more than £100,000.

Tournament organisers will hope they have done enough to stave off the type of player protests that took place at both the French Open and Wimbledon.

The US Open's prize money includes a 2million dollar (approximately £1.5 million) contribution to a new US Open player support programme.

New United States Tennis Association chief executive Craig Tiley, who recently moved from Tennis Australia, said: "This is a significant first step in a multi-year investment in athletes as the US Open continues to be the best economic opportunity for players and the most valuable platform in tennis for players, fans and partners.

"We are proud to deliver record-setting prize money and expanded player benefits as well as providing a new platform to work together with players."

What about Serena Williams' return?

Williams, 44, made her shock return to competition at Wimbledon, where she lost in three sets to Maya Joint before knee trouble forced her to pull out of doubles with her sister, Venus.

A wild card appearance at the Cincinnati Open alongside Venus allowed her to evaluate her knee before deciding to play in the Mixed Doubles Championship alongside Carlos Alcaraz, but she won't be taking part in the women's singles.

Pairing with Alcaraz marks Williams' competitive return to the US Open, at which she last played in 2022.

No! The British No 1 will miss the Grand Slam because of the stress fracture in her right leg that she sustained during the grass-court season and forced her to pull out of Wimbledon.

It has been a frustrating 12 months for Raducanu with more persistent physical issues.

The 2024 semi-finalist will miss this year's tournament as he continues to recover from bone bruising in his left arm.

World No 1 Sabalenka will look to become the first woman to win three straight US Open titles since Serena Williams from 2012-14.

The winners of the singles trophies will each receive 5.5million dollars (approximately £4 million), while first-round prize money has been ramped up to more than £100,000.

Tournament organisers will hope they have done enough to stave off the type of player protests that took place at both the French Open and Wimbledon.

"We are proud to deliver record-setting prize money and expanded player benefits as well as providing a new platform to work together with players."

What about Serena Williams' return?

Williams, 44, made her shock return to competition at Wimbledon, where she lost in three sets to Maya Joint before knee trouble forced her to pull out of doubles with her sister, Venus.

A wild card appearance at the Cincinnati Open alongside Venus allowed her to evaluate her knee before deciding to play in the Mixed Doubles Championship alongside Carlos Alcaraz, but she won't be taking part in the women's singles.

Pairing with Alcaraz marks Williams' competitive return to the US Open, at which she last played in 2022.

articles.title: Nick Kyrgios tests positive for cocaine and is provisionally suspended: Australian tennis player admits to 'huge mistake'
articles.summary: Nick Kyrgios tested positive for benzoylecgonine, a metabolite of cocaine, at an ATP tournament in Majorca in June; the 31-year-old has been provisionally suspended since August 4; he can appeal but the International Tennis Integrity Agency say he "has not done so to date"
articles.body:
Nick Kyrgios has been provisionally suspended after failing a doping test, the International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA) has announced.

The Australian player gave a sample at an ATP tournament in Majorca in June that tested positive for benzoylecgonine, a metabolite of cocaine.

"I made a huge mistake and I take full responsibility for it," Kyrgios said in a post on Instagram on Wednesday.

  • Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream tennis with no contract
  • Download Sky Sports app for analysis, news and video

"I'm sorry to my fans, my family, my sponsors and everyone close to me. Above all, I'm sorry to the kids who follow me. I know the example this sets and I'm deeply disappointed in myself."

Cocaine is banned in competition and former Wimbledon finalist Kyrgios has been provisionally suspended since August 4.

Kyrgios is banned from playing and attending tournaments pending the outcome of a tribunal that will assess his case.

The ITIA said Kyrgios can also appeal the suspension "but has not done so to date".

The 31-year-old, a Wimbledon finalist in 2022, has been plagued by injuries over the last four years which has seen him play only twice in the main draw of a Grand Slam since that run in South West London.

Kyrgios has played just four singles matches this season, adding in his Instagram post that he's felt "helpless and alone" during his battles with injury.

"I'm not going to make excuses, but I do want to give some context about where I've been," he said. "The last couple of years of injuries have taken a huge toll on me, both physically and mentally.

"My body hasn't been able to do what my mind expects it to do, and coming to terms with being near the end of my career has been harder than I ever imagined... letting go of something that has been my whole life is one of the hardest things I've ever had to face.

"At times I've felt helpless and alone. None of that excuses what I did."

Kyrgios is currently ranked 919th in the world. He was given a wild card to play doubles at Wimbledon last month and lost in the first round with partner Alexander Bublik.

'Tormented soul' Kyrgios in firing line

Sky Sports Tennis' Annabel Croft described Kyrgios as a "tormented soul" who could now find himself on the receiving end of the very criticism he dished out when Jannik Sinner and Iga Swiatek were involved in high-profile doping cases.

"He has always struck me as a tormented soul out there, and he is never far from creating headlines," Croft said. "He seems to do that effortlessly.

"There is a lot of criticism being thrown at him right now because he was the one firing arrows at other players who had been banned for a certain amount of time. It is now being directed right back at him."

'Kyrgios needs to find balance'

Former world No 40 Ryan Harrison believes Kyrgios must strike the right balance between his responsibilities on the court and his downtime off it.

"It is disappointing," Harrison added. "Kyrgios has been such an electric player for so long.

"He is one of those guys. You talk about the 'Big Four', and he was the next in line that the casual fan and observer would talk about because of the way he played, his talent, fearlessness and energy.

"The persona would come out sometimes in the way he handled pressure. Sometimes it wasn't always positive.

"When you are an athlete and training on a regular basis, your life is very structured and regimented.

"When you stop playing and you are not doing that on a week-to-week basis, some players can find it difficult to strike a balance and know, 'When can I go out?'

"I think Nick needs to find that balance and, while it is disappointing, hopefully for his sake, as he takes time away, he can find happiness off the court and be the best he can be."

Controversial Kyrgios' career timeline

  • 2013: Turns professional after winning the Australian Open boys' singles title in January of that year
  • 2014: Announces himself to the world on his Wimbledon debut by upsetting world No 1 Rafael Nadal in the fourth round when just 19 years old.
  • July 2015: Criticised for his behaviour and comments at Wimbledon, including accusations of 'tanking' in fourth-round loss to Richard Gasquet.
  • August 2015: Fined and given 28-day suspended ban for controversial comments about Stan Wawrinka's then-girlfriend, women's player Donna Vekic.
  • October 2016: Criticised for his effort during a defeat to Mischa Zverev at Shanghai Masters. Receives an eight-week suspension, which was later reduced.
  • October 2016: Reaches his career-high singles ranking of 13th in the world in October after claiming his first three of seven career ATP titles in the same year - wins in Marseille, Atlanta, and Tokyo.
  • June 2018: Fined for inappropriate behaviour during Queen's semi-final match against Marin Cilic after TV cameras caught him using his water bottle to simulate a lewd act during a changeover.
  • May 2019: Throws a chair onto the court during the Rome Masters and is defaulted from his match against Casper Ruud.
  • January 2022: Wins the Australian Open men's doubles title with fellow Australian and good friend Thanasi Kokkinakis.
  • July 2022: Reaches his first Grand Slam singles final at Wimbledon, which he loses in four sets to Novak Djokovic. His run is not without controversy as he is twice fined for his behaviour, for spitting towards a spectator in his first-round match with Paul Jubb and for an audible obscenity during a fiery third-round encounter with Stefanos Tsitsipas.
  • January 2023: Undergoes knee surgery, beginning a prolonged period of injury problems that has limited him to only one Grand Slam appearance since.
  • February 2023: Has an assault charge dismissed by a magistrate after pleading guilty to shoving over his ex-girlfriend in 2021.
  • July 2023: Withdraws from Wimbledon because of a wrist injury, having hoped to match or even improve on his run to the final the prior year.
  • August 2026: Provisionally suspended after a sample given at an ATP tournament in Majorca in June tested positive for benzoylecgonine, a metabolite of cocaine.

articles.title: Cincinnati Open: Top seeds Aryna Sabalenka and Alexander Zverev stunned in last 16 as Coco Gauff progresses to quarter-finals
articles.summary: Both top seeds in the women's and men's draw fall in the last 16 of Cincinnati Open as Aryna Sabalenka and Alexander Zverev suffer defeats; watch the US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis from August 30
articles.body:
World No 1 Aryna Sabalenka has been knocked out of the Cincinnati Open after suffering a shock straight-sets defeat to Czech player Sara Bejlek.

The 35th-ranked and unseeded Bejlek defeated the four-time Grand Slam champion Sabalanka 7-6 (7) 6-4 in just under two hours to advance to the quarter-finals of the WTA 1000 event.

Bejlek rallied from 5-1 down in a first-set tiebreaker then came from 4-1 behind in the second set to clinch her first career victory over a top-10 opponent.

  • Download Sky Sports app for analysis, news and video

The 20-year-old from Znojmo will next face Madison Keys in the quarter-finals.

Bejlek was left speechless at what she had achieved.

"I feel incredible. I lost totally my words," she said on court after the match. "I just kept believing and that was the key today."

Sabalenka's defeat means Elena ⁠Rybakina can replace her as world ⁠No 1 by reaching the Cincinnati final.

Coco Gauff advanced to the quarter-finals after sweeping past 22nd-seeded Czech Marie Bouzkova 6-3 6-2.

The fourth-seeded Gauff needed just one-hour and 33 minutes to progress and will face Ukraine's Marta Kostyuk next for a spot in the semi-finals.

Paul beats top seed Zverev as Tiafoe beats second seed Auger-Aliassime

Tommy Paul saved ‌a match point to defeat top seed Alexander Zverev ‌4-6 7-6(6) 6-4 and reach the quarter-finals of ​the Cincinnati Open after a nearly 90-minute rain delay.

Zverev took ‌the first set and trailed 3-4 in the ​second before the fourth-round match was suspended due to rain.

Paul emerged from the lengthy ​delay looking the sharper ⁠player, saving a match ⁠point before levelling the contest as Zverev struggled to find ‌his rhythm.

The German took a 4-2 lead in the third set but Paul ‌dug his heels in to take control of the match, rallying to win four straight games in a stunning comeback to ⁠advance to the quarter-finals in ​Cincinnati for the first time.

He will face Flavio Cobolli in the quarter-finals.

Frances Tiafoe notched a milestone victory when he delivered one of the most composed performances of his season to upset second seed Felix Auger-Aliassime 6-4 6-4 at the ATP Masters 1000 event.

With the victory, the 28-year-old advanced to his second Masters 1000 quarter-final of the season, having also reached the last eight in Miami. It is the first time in his career that Tiafoe has reached multiple Masters 1000 quarter-finals in a single season.

The American will next face Lorenzo Musetti, who defeated Jaime Faria 7-5 6-2 in 75 minutes.

Arthur Fils also made his mark as he came through with a 6-3 6-4 win over fifth seed Alex De Minaur.

Taylor Fritz, the highest-ranked American man remaining in the tournament, beat Australian Christopher O'Connell in straight sets, 6-4 6-3.

Meanwhile, Thiago Tirante, who beat Novak Djokovic in the second round, became the first Argentine to reach the quarters in Cincinnati since Juan Martín del Potro in 2018 with a 5-7 6-4 6-4 win over Jakub Mensik.

articles.title: Carlos Alcaraz to Return from Injury for 2026 US Open After Missing Wimbledon, Roland-Garros
articles.summary: Carlos Alcaraz confirmed Thursday that he will return from a wrist injury to play in the 2026 U.S. Open.
articles.body:
Carlos Alcaraz confirmed Thursday that he will return from a wrist injury to play in the 2026 U.S. Open.

Alcaraz made his return official in a joint Instagram post with world football insider Fabrizio Romano. "Here we go! Carlos Alcaraz will return to the tour at the U.S. Open after spending four months sidelined with a right wrist injury," Romano wrote.

Agassi, Serena and more iconic US Open outfits

The 23-year-old Alcaraz took to X to share the news as well on the heels of missing both the French Open and Wimbledon:

A seven-time Grand Slam singles champion, Alcaraz last played in the Barcelona Open back in April.

Alcaraz withdrew from the tournament due to a wrist injury after winning his first-round matchup, and that led to a prolonged absence that saw him miss both Roland-Garros in May and June, and Wimbledon in June and July.

The only Grand Slam tournament Alcaraz has played thus far in 2026 is the Australian Open. The Spaniard was victorious, allowing him to complete the career Grand Slam by winning all four major tournaments.

With Alcaraz out of the fold, Alexander Zverev won his first career Grand Slam at the French Open, while world No. 1 Jannik Sinner triumphed at Wimbledon.

Despite having not played a tournament in four months, Alcaraz is still No. 2 in the ATP rankings behind only Sinner, putting him in position to be among the top seeds at the U.S. Open.

In five career appearances in the U.S. Open singles tournament, Alcaraz has made it to at least the quarterfinals on four occasions.

He won the 2022 U.S. Open, marking the first Grand Slam singles title of his career, and Alcaraz is also the reigning U.S. Open champ, beating Sinner in last year's final.

Scheduled to start on Aug. 30, Alcaraz doesn't have much time to get back in rhythm ahead of the U.S. Open, but he promises to be among the top contenders nonetheless.

In five career appearances in the U.S. Open singles tournament, Alcaraz has made it to at least the quarterfinals on four occasions.
He won the 2022 U.S. Open, marking the first Grand Slam singles title of his career, and Alcaraz is also the reigning U.S. Open champ, beating Sinner in last year's final.
Scheduled to start on Aug. 30, Alcaraz doesn't have much time to get back in rhythm ahead of the U.S. Open, but he promises to be among the top contenders nonetheless.

articles.summary: El murciano parte este fin de semana hacia Nueva York y preparará a conciencia el US Open en Flushing Meadows

articles.title: Rafa Jódar, el mejor a los 50 partidos
articles.standfirst: El madrileño mejora las cifras del 'Big Three', Alcaraz y Sinner, con un balance de 36 victorias y 14 derrotas
articles.summary: El madrileño mejora las cifras del 'Big Three', Alcaraz y Sinner, con un balance de 36 victorias y 14 derrotas
articles.body: A pesar de la eliminación en los octavos de Cincinnati a manos de Flavio Cobolli, Rafa Jódar mejora las estadísticas de los más grandes en su primera temporada como profesional. El joven madrileño, de tan sólo 19 años, presenta el mejor balance en la Era Open después de haber disputado sus primeros 50 partidos oficiales (no se cuentan los dos triunfos de las Next Gen Finals). Rafa cuenta con un balance de 36 victorias por 14 derrotas, el mismo registro que en su día firmó el argentino José Luis Clerc. La nueva sensación del tenis mundial mejora las cifras de Carlos Alcaraz, Jannik Sinner y el Big Three al llegar al medio centenar de duelos en el circuito. Alcaraz y Rafael Nadal tenían 31 triunfos, por los 30 de Sinner y los 27 de Roger Federer y Novak Djokovic. Los que más cerca están de Jódar en esa estadística son John McEnroe, Andy Roddick, Andrei Medvedev y Guillermo Párez Roldán, con 34 partidos ganados. Rafa, que pagó ante Cobolli el cansancio de una gira americana que para él empezó el 27 de julio en Washington —alcanzó las semifinales—, tendrá un mínimo descanso antes de preparar el asalto al US Open (30 de agosto al 13 de septiembre). Su primera sesión preparatoria en Nueva York será el martes 25 de agosto. Acumula ya 64 partidos jugados en 2026, de los que 13 corresponden a la actual gira norteamericana de superficie dura.

articles.title: Jannik Sinner confirma su baja para el US Open: "Estoy muy triste y decepcionado"
articles.standfirst: El italiano ha comunicado en redes sociales que "aún necesito más tiempo para recuperarme de mi problema en la rodilla derecha"
articles.summary: El italiano ha comunicado en redes sociales que "aún necesito más tiempo para recuperarme de mi problema en la rodilla derecha"
articles.body: Jannik Sinner anunció este viernes que no disputará el próximo US Open por problemas físicos. El italiano, que pasó a principios de agosto varios exámenes médicos para dilucidar si llegaba en condiciones óptimas al último Grand Slam del año, ha confirmado que no estará en el cuadro individual del torneo de Nueva York. "Aunque he estado trabajando duro con mi equipo y mi personal médico, ahora hemos tenido que tomar la difícil decisión de que no podré competir en el US Open de este año", aseguró en sus redes sociales. Sinner, que no disputa ningún encuentro desde que se coronara ganador en Wimbledon por segundo año consecutivo, explicó que "hemos vuelto a la pista en Montecarlo durante los últimos días y nos hemos dado cuenta de que aún necesito más tiempo para recuperarme de mi problema en la rodilla derecha". El italiano ya se había dado de baja de los Masters 1000 de Montreal y Cincinnati. Su ausencia definitiva se produce un día después de que Carlos Alcaraz anunciara su regreso cuatro meses después. El español ha estado alejando de las pistas por una lesión en la muñeca derecha que sufrió en abril, durante el torneo Conde de Godó de Barcelona. El italiano se mostró apesadumbrado por su ausencia en el último Grand Slam de la temporada: "Obviamente estoy muy triste y decepcionado, ya que Nueva York ocupa un lugar especial en mi corazón. Estaba muy ilusionado con regresar y jugar en la electrizante atmósfera frente a los grandes aficionados allí".

articles.standfirst: La polaca ya está en semifinales de Cincinnati tras la retirada de una Rybakina que ya no podrá optar al número uno en Estados Unidos
articles.summary: La polaca ya está en semifinales de Cincinnati tras la retirada de una Rybakina que ya no podrá optar al número uno en Estados Unidos
articles.body: Iga Swiatek le ha hecho un "favor" a Aryna Sabalenka tras su clasificación a las semifinales del TMS de Ohio. La actual reina del circuito conservará su condición como número uno, al menos de cara al US Open ante la retirada de Elena Rybakina cuando perdía por 4-1 en el primer set. Un desenlace que pocos querían para el que tenía todas las papeletas de ser el mejor encuentro del torneo. Iga entró a la pista en modo máquina. Salvó una bola de 'break' en el juego inicial y acto seguido aprovechó su primera oportunidad para, no solo romper el saque, sino también todos los esquemas de la kazaja. El tremendo trabajo de pies de la polaca, clave en el inicio. En el sexto juego Rybakina decía adiós al partido y a sus opciones de ser número 1 (tenía que llegar a la final para conseguirlo). Notó molestias en su pierna izquierda en mitad de un intercambio, dolores que persistieron en el saque posterior y obligaron a la kazaja a abandonar cuando cedía por 4-1 en 28 minutos. La segunda raqueta mundial hace saltar todas las alarmas de cara al último grande del año que empieza en tan solo cuatro días (del 25 de agosto al 13 de septiembre). Debido a su pase a la penúltima ronda del certamen americano, Iga Swiatek ya es la tercera jugadora con más apariciones en semifinales de Masters 1000, firma 24. Siendo solo superada por Serena Williams (26) y Simona Halep (29). Tiempo al tiempo de que las supere. Se las verá con Jessica Pegula por un pase a la final. En el apartado masculino, el francés Arthur Fils acabó con la gran semana del argentino Tirante, verdugo de Djokovic, Landaluce y Mensik, y jugará sus terceras semifinales de Masters 1000 ante Flavio Cobolli. El italiano derrotó a Tommy Paul en tres mangas en los cuartos de final. En caso de que el diestro de Florencia venza en su duelo de semifinales, le arrebatará a Novak Djokovic el quinto puesto del ranking ATP y quedará virtualmente entre los cinco mejores.

articles.title: Jannik Sinner Out of 2026 US Open with Knee Injury, World No. 1 Explains Decision in Statement
articles.summary: Jannik Sinner has withdrawn from the 2026 U.S. Open due to a knee injury.
articles.body:
Jannik Sinner has withdrawn from the 2026 U.S. Open due to a knee injury.

The U.S. Open officially announced Sinner's withdrawal from the tournament and Carlos Taberner will be added to the main draw.

In a statement on X, Sinner explained the right knee injury that has kept him out since winning Wimbledon has yet not recovered to the point that he is ready to play in a full tournament.

Agassi, Serena and more iconic US Open outfits

Sinner withdrew from the Canadian Open that began on Aug. 2 due to what he described as "health reasons." He was also scheduled to take part in the Cincinnati Open, but wound up skipping the event to rest and recover.

The last time Sinner played was on July 12 when he defeated Alexander Zverev in the Wimbledon gentlemen's final to win his second straight title at the All England Club.

Sinner, currently the No. 1 player in the ATP rankings, would have been the top seed at the U.S. Open when the draw is announced on Aug. 27.

Instead, the honor could go to Carlos Alcaraz in his return to competition. The 23-year-old announced on Thursday he will play in the U.S. Open after missing four months due to a wrist injury.

Alcaraz last played at the Barcelona Open when he had to withdraw prior to a second-round match against Tomáš Macháč. He is looking for his second Grand Slam tournament victory of the season after winning the Australian Open in February.

This will be the first major tournament Sinner hasn't played since the 2019 French Open when he was still playing primarily on the Challenger Tour.

Sinner reached the final at the U.S. Open in each of the previous two years. He won in 2024 by defeating Taylor Fritz, then lost to Alcaraz in four sets last year.

The 2026 U.S. Open begins on Aug. 30 and runs through Sept. 13.

He missed the Masters 1000 events in Canada and Cincinnati, pulling out of the latter with a right knee injury to focus on being ready to play at Flushing Meadows, but has confirmed he will be unable to feature in New York.

In a statement on social media, 2024 champion Sinner said: "Even though I have been working hard with my team and my medical staff, we have now had to make the difficult decision that I will not be able to compete at the US Open this year.

"We have been back on court in Monte Carlo over the last couple of days and have realised that I still need more time to recover from my right knee issue.

"I'm obviously very sad and disappointed, as New York has a special place in my heart. I was very much looking forward to coming back and playing in the electric atmosphere in front of the great fans there."

Sinner's withdrawal comes a day after his great rival Carlos Alcaraz, who the Italian lost to in the final 12 months ago, revealed he will make his comeback from four months out with a wrist injury.

"It's a big blow to tennis because it feels like a long time ago that we had Alcaraz and Sinner in the events together and it feels like a great loss."

Croft continued: "It also underlines how relentless and demanding the tour is physically. When you think at the beginning of the year when he won those five back-to-back Masters 1000 titles which was absolutely exceptional and a phenomenal achievement, but when he got to Roland-Garros there was not much left in the tank and it cost him perhaps the French Open title..

"Then we saw him rebound at Wimbledon which he built with each match but once again his body has let himself down. For all of these players it's such a difficult balance. You keep trying to play the tour, play the mandatory events but you also want to peak at the Grand Slams and it's not quite happening at the moment."

Former world No 40 Ryan Harrison added: "Sinner feels the risk of playing the US Open is a little bit too much."

Croft said: "It's a long time since we had them in the same draw [since Monte Carlo]. They have become the new rivalry that everyone wants to see. I really don't mind watching the same players compete all the time because those are the matches you really look forward to.

"It's like watching a big boxing fight. You want to see the very best go up against each other, but now it's an opportunity for the next category down to shine. It's interesting because it's a bit of a transitional period at the moment.

"Who knows what will happen when we get them all back together."

articles.title: Cincinnati Open: Coco Gauff races into semi-finals as USA eye titles in men's and women's tournaments
articles.summary: Coco Gauff reached her fifth WTA 1000 semi-final of 2026, as Frances Tiafoe and Brandon Nakashima lined up a last-four cracker in the men's tournament; Watch the US Open from August 30 live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, streaming service NOW and the Sky Sports app
articles.body:
Coco Gauff swept into the semi-finals of the Cincinnati Open with a 70-minute dismantling of Marta Kostyuk.

The 22-year-old's 6-2 6-2 win over the Ukrainian carried her into a fifth WTA 1000 semi-final of the year and a second in Cincinnati, where she lifted the title in 2023.

  • Alcaraz to make his return at US Open

  • Not got Sky? Get Sky Sports or stream with no contract 📱

Standing between Gauff and another final is the tournament's giant-killer.

Sara Bejlek, the unseeded 20-year-old who stunned world No 1 Aryna Sabalenka in straight sets in the last 16, came from a set down to beat 2019 champion Madison Keys 3-6 6-4 7-6 (7-5) and reach the first WTA 1000 semi-final of her career.

"Sara is a great player," Gauff said. "I watched her a lot in Abu Dhabi this year when she won that title. So I think it's going to be a tough match. I'm looking forward to it."

Bejlek, who won that Abu Dhabi Open title back in February when she was ranked outside the world's top 100, believes her mentality has improved now when facing the top echelon of players in the women's game.

"I believe in myself much more than I ever have before," said the rising Czech star.

World No 3 Jessica Pegula beat Amanda Anisimova in a third set tie-break on Thursday and faces world No 5 and defending champion Iga Swiatek in the other semi-final.

With two Americans also in the semis of the men's singles, Gauff is dreaming of a home sweep this week.

"It's insane, I think we're all doing so well," she said. "Hopefully we can have a double title win. Obviously there are more matches to be played for that to happen. We definitely root for each other."

Tiafoe and Nakashima book first all-US men's semi since 2010

In the men's draw, Frances Tiafoe and Brandon Nakashima made history of their own, becoming the first two Americans to reach the Cincinnati semi-finals since Andy Roddick and Mardy Fish in 2010.

Tiafoe, the 2024 runner-up to Jannik Sinner, needed more than two hours and four match points to see off 10th seed Lorenzo Musetti 7-6 (7-2) 7-5 on a humid Ohio night, firing 18 winners before sealing it with an unreturnable serve as he looks to revive a summer disrupted by a wrist injury and early exits in Washington and Montreal.

Nakashima recovered from a break down in the deciding set to beat sixth seed Taylor Fritz 7-6 (11-9) 4-6 6-3, a fourth top-10 win of the season that makes him the first American man to reach the semi-finals in Canada and Cincinnati in the same year since Mardy Fish in 2011.

Nakashima, who has won just one of his seven professional encounters with his compatriot, is coached by Tiafoe's former coach Wayne Ferreira.

Tiafoe believes both players will know exactly what to expect from each other heading into their last four clash.

"It's a guy who knows me pretty well in Wayne," Tiafoe said. "I expect some good serving and all the best from him. Happy where I've been mentally more than anything. This has been a great week."

Italy's Flavio Cobolli faces Frenchman Arthur Fils in the other men's semi-final, with the US Open beginning later this month, live on Sky Sports.

articles.title: Alcaraz y Serena, 46 'Grand Slam' juntos en el mixto del US Open
articles.standfirst: Se confirma la pareja estrella del torneo junto a la que forman Djokovic y Sabalenka
articles.summary: Se confirma la pareja estrella del torneo junto a la que forman Djokovic y Sabalenka
articles.body: El nuevo US Open mixto, en la segunda edición que se programa la semana previa al inicio de los cuadros individuales, contará con una pareja que seguro llenará las gradas de la central Arthur Ashe, el estadio de tenis más grande del mundo con capacidad para más de 23.000 aficionados.  Lo que era un secreto a voces se ha confirmado oficialmente y Carlos Alcaraz y Serena Williams, separados por 22 años, se juntarán en un dúo histórico que suma 46 títulos del Grand Slam. Serena cuenta con 39 (23 individuales, 14 dobles y dos en mixtos) por los siete del fenómeno de El Palmar.  Los dos triunfos en mixtos de la leyenda estadounidense fueron con el bielorruso Max Mirnyi, en Wimbledon y el Abierto de los Estados Unidos, en 1998. Mirnyi es en la actualidad uno de los entrenadores de Sabalenka, número uno del circuito femenino.  Los otros dos grandes nombres que formarán juntos son Novak Djokovic (24 'majors') y Aryna Sabalenka, con seis grandes en su palmarés, entre individuales (4) y dobles (2).  Otros participantes destacados son Alexander Zverev y Taylor Townsend; Felix Auger-Aliassime y Alexandra Eala; Iga Swiatek al lado de Casper Ruud; o Flavio Cobolli con Belinda Bencic.  El cuadro principal estará compuesto por un total de 16 equipos y se disputará los días 25 y 26, con rondas de eliminación directa a partir de octavos. Los partidos son al mejor de tres sets (cuatro juegos por set) y un súper 'tie break' en caso de tener que acudir al desempate.  El lunes 24 se jugará la fase previa del certamen con ocho dúos y dos billetes en juego para unirse a los 14 clasificados directamente. Alcaraz y Serena, que no estaban apuntados en la lista inicial, han recibido una de las tres invitaciones de la organización. Carlitos participó en la edición de 2025 junto a Emma Raducanu. Cedieron en el debut ante Jessica Pegula y Jack Draper.  Dentro de la cifra récord en premios del US Open 2026, que se eleva a 108 millones de dólares, un millón irá destinados a la pareja campeona del atractivo mixto. Sólo por participar son 40.000 dólares. Los cuartos valen 120.000; las semifinales 250.000 y los finalistas se embolsarán medio millón a repartir.  Alcaraz volverá a competir de manera oficial 133 días después de la lesión en la muñeca derecha, que se produjo en su debut en el Barcelona Open Banc Sabadell con el finlandés Otto Virtanen.

articles.title: Cincinnati Open: Coco Gauff and Jessica Pegula to meet in tournament's first all-American women's final in 56 years
articles.summary: Jessica Pegula topples defending champion Iga Swiatek in her semi-final; fellow American Frances Tiafoe also reaches men's final and faces France's Arthur Fils; watch the US Open from August 30 live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, NOW and the Sky Sports app
articles.body:
The Cincinnati Open will host its first all-American women's final in 56 years after Coco Gauff and Jessica Pegula won their respective semi-finals.

Fourth seed Gauff cruised home in her clash with Sara Bejlek, eclipsing the Czech 6-4 6-1, while third seed Pegula earned her spot by toppling defending champion Iga Swiatek 7-5 4-6 6-4.

The last Cincinnati Open final to feature two American women came in 1970 when Rosie Casals defeated Nancy Richey.

Fellow American Frances Tiafoe also reached the men's final, where he will face France's Arthur Fils.

Pegula dethrones Swiatek to secure Gauff final

Pegula rallied from a break down in the deciding ‌set to defeat six-time Grand Slam champion Swiatek in her semi-final.

World No 3 Pegula and seventh seed Swiatek traded breaks early in ​the opening set before rain briefly interrupted play with the score level at 1-1.

Swiatek ‌clawed her way back, breaking to level at 4-4 before moving ahead, but with the set locked at 5-5, Pegula capitalised ​on a Swiatek double fault to break for 6-5 before the Pole sent the simplest of smashes into the net to hand Pegula the opener.

In the second set, Swiatek was more aggressive, breaking in the ⁠sixth game to take a 4-2 lead.

Pegula broke back and managed to level the contest, but the former world No 1 levelled things up when Pegula missed a forehand return.

Pegula refused to fade after Swiatek moved 3-1 ahead in the decider. The American levelled at 4-4, earned the decisive break in the ‌next game and then served out for a memorable victory.

"It was a really tough match. She (Swiatek) is in great form. To beat someone who is such a great athlete like Iga in the semis and to make it to another 1000 final, it's ⁠awesome," Pegula said.

She will face Gauff in the final after the two-time Grand Slam winner made light work of unseeded Czech ​Bejlek in the last four.

The 20-year-old had stunned world No 1 Aryna Sabalenka and Madison Keys en route to booking her first WTA 1000 semi-final spot.

Gauff proved superior in the opening set, earning a 4-1 lead after breaking serve early on.

However, Bejlek managed to stay in contention and level at 4-4. It wouldn't be enough to stop the 22-year-old, however, who broke serve again before closing out the set.

Gauff then broke twice more in the second set, capitalising on a catalogue of Bejlek unforced ​errors to seal victory in 76 minutes.

Impressive Fils faces Tiafoe in men's final

Frenchman Fils produced a commanding ‌67-minute display to sweep aside seventh seed Flavio Cobolli ‌6-3 6-4 on Saturday and secure his ​place in the men's final in Cincinnati.

The 21st seed recovered ​quickly after Cobolli broke for ‌a 2-1 lead, breaking straight back to level ​at 2-2.

With the opening set locked at 3-3, Fils improved his performance ​to take a 4-3 lead ⁠before breaking decisively ⁠in the eighth game as Cobolli misfired from the ‌baseline.

Fils, who won the Barcelona Open in April, maintained his momentum in the ‌second set, breaking serve in the opening game.

Cobolli held to love at 4-3 to keep the pressure on but ⁠Fils proved superior, dictating play ​with sharp forehands to ​gain a 5-4 lead and ultimately ​clinch victory, having scored 22 winners ⁠and six aces.

"I was very happy with the performance," Fils said. "I started pretty slow. I was a bit tight, but I think from 4-3 in the first set when I won those long rallies, just the momentum came my way and I felt so much better."

Fils has risen 10 spots to No 11 in the ATP live rankings as a result of his run to the final, where he will face Tiafoe after he beat fellow American ​Brandon Nakashima 7-5 6-3 in their semi-final..

The pair traded four consecutive breaks before drawing level at 3-3 in the opening set, ​but Tiafoe held to love in the seventh game and broke again to move 6-5 ahead before serving out the set.

The 27-year-old broke Nakashima for a 3-2 lead in the second set ‌and would go on to clinch victory with another impressive hold to love.

articles.body: La organización del US Open ha convertido el último Grand Slam en un torneo de tres semanas. Después de lograr que la competición gane un día y empiece en domingo, como Roland Garros y el Open de Australia, ahora han convertido la semana de los aficionados en una gran fiesta.  Además de la tradicional fase previa, en las pistas del Billie Jean King Tennis Center, concretamente en las dos pistas principales, la Arthur Ashe y la Louis Armstrong, se celebrará los días 25 y 26 de agosto la segunda edición del revolucionario mixto del Abierto de los Estados Unidos.  Para fomentar la participación de las grandes figuras se adelantan las fechas y se reduce el torneo a dos días y 16 equipos. articles.summary: El murciano aterrizó el sábado en Nueva York y este domingo realizó su primera práctica
articles.body: N o hay tiempo que perder para Carlos Alcaraz. El campeón de siete grandes, que viajó la mañana del sábado a Nueva York, desde Madrid, ya se ejercita este domingo en las pistas de Flushing Meadows para preparar su regreso a la competición oficial. Lo ha hecho practicando al lado de Samuel López y Álvaro Alcaraz.  Cuando salte a jugar el dobles mixto al lado de Serena Williams, el próximo martes 25 de agosto, habrán pasado 133 días desde la lesión en la muñeca derecha en la primera ronda del Barcelona Open Banc Sabadell.  Carlitos practicó este domingo en la cancha Louis Armstrong, la segunda en importancia del Billie Jean King Tennis Center, por detrás de la Arthur Ashe. La última vez que el tenista de El Palmar pisó la instalación fue el 7 de septiembre de 2025 cuando se impuso en la final a Jannik Sinner.  En la sesión, utilizó siempre una gorra ante los gritos de admiración de cientos de aficionados que no se quisieron perder los primeros golpes de Alcaraz en la ciudad de los rascacielos.  El murciano ha salido del túnel de vestuarios seguido por Juanjo López, su médico y que ha estado atento a todos los movimientos del tenista en pista.

articles.summary: El suizo disputará un partido de individuales y otro de dobles en la semana previa al torneo
articles.body: Flushing Meadows volverá a disfrutar de Roger Federer en una pista de tenis. El campeón de 20 Grand Slam regresará a Nueva York para formar parte de la 'fan week' previa al cuadro principal del US Open.  El evento contará con la presencia de Roger Federer, Andy Roddick, John McEnroe y Andre Agassi, cuatro campeones de Grand Slam. La organización ha anunciado la disputa de un partido de individuales entre el suizo y Roddick a un set, sin ventajas. Y un segundo encuentro de dobles (Federer y McEnroe ante Roddick y Agassi) con el mismo formato. Todo esto sucederá el sábado 29 de agosto, un día antes del inicio de los cuadros masculino y femenino. articles.body:
Frenchman Arthur Fils may have played himself into contention to win the US Open after sealing the biggest title of his career at the Cincinnati Open on Sunday.

The 21st seed, who won the Barcelona Open in April, added the Cincy crown to his growing list of achievements with a topsy-turvy 6-3 1-6 6-0 victory over Frances Tiafoe in Ohio.

Fils became the third Black man to win a Masters 1000 title, joining Ben Shelton, who won the Canadian Open twice, and Jo-Wilfried Tsonga, who won Paris in 2008 and Canada in 2014.

"That feels good," said Fils, who dominated the deciding set to end France's 12-year wait for a Masters 1000 title. "There's a lot of training, a lot of sacrifice. Injury. To be able to win a title like this, it means a lot to me.

"I don't have any words to describe this. It feels so good. A little bit of relief as well."

Fils made a flying start by breaking early to establish a 3-0 ​lead in the opening set before ‌Tiafoe got on the board with a hold of serve.

The ​Frenchman maintained relentless pressure from the baseline, attacking Tiafoe's second serve and forcing errors as he moved ​5-3 ahead. Fils was untouchable on ⁠serve, closing out the ⁠set with three successive aces without dropping a point in the final ‌game.

Tiafoe, playing in his second Cincinnati final, responded in kind in the second set.

The 28-year-old broke in ‌the second game en route to a 3-0 lead, with his forehands pulling Fils wide. Although Fils got on the board with a hold to ⁠love, the 17th seed Tiafoe broke ​again for a 5-1 advantage before forcing ​a decider.

Fils quickly regained control in ​the third set, breaking twice to race into ⁠a 4-0 lead as Tiafoe's backhand errors piled up.

The 22-year-old's pace and movement proved too much ⁠for the American, and he ​closed out the match with a bagel ​final set after a lengthy rally to lift the trophy.

Tale of the Tape

Now 32-10 for the year, Fils is up eight spots to fifth in the ATP Live Race To Turin as a result of his run.

'Fils is like a ballet dancer'

Annabel Croft, speaking on Sky Sports Tennis:

"He talked about the sacrifices he made and the injuries he has had but what a performance that was in the final set. He played flawless tennis in the first set but he regrouped so well in that final set and breath-taking movement to watch him courtside.

"He's so agile, he's like a ballet dancer, and we saw every kind of shot that he could possibly come up with to win this title and to take on a home crowd as well it was really impressive."

Croft added: "He's so mature on the court. He's physically very mature and that was the aspect for me just how well this guy moves across the court. It's very dynamic. It's the take-off speed but it's also the agility. He can be on the front foot and attacking, but when he's pushed defensively he can turn on a sixpence and then put in the slices and defend so well."

articles.summary: In the first all-American women's final in Cincinnati for 56 years, Coco Gauff cruised to a 6-2 6-4 victory over Jessica Pegula; watch the US Open from August 30 live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, streaming service NOW and the Sky Sports app
articles.body:
Coco Gauff defeated fellow American Jessica Pegula in straight sets, 6-2 6-4, to capture her second Cincinnati Open women's singles title.

It means the world No 4 becomes just the third player in the Open Era, after Serena Williams and Victoria Azarenka, to win multiple titles in Cincinnati.

Pegula had beaten defending champion Iga Swiatek in the semi-finals, while Gauff disposed of unseeded Sara Bejlek - who had knocked out world No 1 Aryna Sabalenka - to set up the first all-American women's final in Cincinnati for 56 years.

  • Download Sky Sports app for analysis, news and video 📺
  • Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream with no contract on NOW📱

Gauff stormed out to a 5-0 lead in the first set, taking it 6-2. Pegula battled back to 5-4 in the second before Gauff, who converted five out of six break points in the contest, closed out the win.

"I think it was a long journey, but I'm happy," Gauff said. "I think it's night and day, the player I was last year to now.

"I don't think that this is an indicator that I'm going to do well in New York [at the US Open]. Just knowing the quality wins that I had this week, hopefully I can use that experience."

Gauff had five wins in straight sets in Cincinnati.

"I thought she just played at a really high level and didn't really have many dips," Pegula said. "I didn't really think I played bad.

"The more you construct the point [against her], the worse it is because she almost likes to run. It was tough today. A dangerous, confident Coco is going to New York."

The head-to-head series between Gauff and Pegula is now tied at five apiece. Sunday was their second meeting in a final, with Gauff winning at Wuhan last year.

articles.title: US Open Tennis: Alex Eala is the biggest thing to come out of the Philippines since legendary boxer Manny Pacquiao
articles.summary: Alex Eala achieved a big milestone by claiming the Washington Open but what are her chances in New York? Watch the US Open from August 30 live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, streaming service NOW and the Sky Sports app
articles.body:
"Once it grows, it cannot be stopped" - tennis superstar-in-the-making Alex Eala is quickly becoming the biggest thing to come out of the Philippines since legendary boxer Manny Pacquiao.

The 21-year-old is carrying the hopes of a nation, the volume of support when she plays calling to mind the days when world boxing champion 'Pac Man' put the country on the map as a sporting force.

Few young players on the WTA Tour have experienced the level of expectation and support Eala has received ‌since she earned a place on the circuit, and she showed what all the fuss is about ‌by winning the recent Washington Open.

  • Latest tennis scores and results 🎾
  • Download Sky Sports app for analysis, news and video 📺
  • Not got Sky? Get Sky Sports or stream with no contract 📱

After a run to the fourth round of Wimbledon, which included a victory over defending champion Iga Swiatek, Eala capped her breakthrough in the US capital by rallying to defeat top seed Jessica Pegula 4-6 ​6-4 6-0 in a rain-interrupted final, becoming the first woman from her country to claim a tour-level singles crown.

Along the way, ​she beat Olympic champion Zheng Qinwen, last year's winner Leylah ‌Fernandez, second seed Elina Svitolina and four-time Grand Slam champion Naomi Osaka.

Her remarkable run of victories mark her down out as a ​dangerous outsider for the US Open, starting August 30 - live on Sky Sports.

"It's an incredible milestone for me," said Eala, who moved to Spain to attend the Rafa Nadal Academy on a scholarship at the age of 13. "Coming into the tournament, I knew that the competition was super strong and my draw was quite tough. Every match was a ‌different set of obstacles. I'm really proud.

"I ended the tournament in better shape than I started. Each match I kept improving and kept learning things about myself. So it definitely gives me ‌a lot of confidence.

"It's really nice to see all the things I've been working on off court or during training being implemented in matches."

Rise of the Filipino superstar-in-waiting

Eala's progress has been closely watched since her US Open junior triumph in 2022, and she reached the Eastbourne final last year before making the fourth ⁠round at Wimbledon - signalling a steady improvement.

As Eala's reputation grew, so ​too did her following, with large groups of Filipino fans packing ​the stands at tournaments around the world to back a player many see ​as a pioneer for tennis in their country.

Her popularity - like Pacquiao in his heyday - was evident in the final ⁠of the WTA 500 event in Washington. By the time the tournament ended, the phrase written across the Nike T-shirt she had worn earlier that week had become a reality: "Once it grows, it cannot be stopped."

Philippines president Ferdinand Marcos released a message on social media congratulating Eala on "yet another historic achievement", adding: "You continue to redefine what is possible for Philippine tennis and inspire countless young Filipinos to dream without limits."

The Philippines' sporting interests have historically been all about basketball, billiards and boxing, but the nation is now being swept up in tennis fever.

'Eala is class with a awkward lefty serve'

Sky Sports analyst Annabel Croft believes Eala can be one of the "biggest stars" and is "just what the tour needs" following her success in Washington.

The former British No 1 said: "I've never seen anything like it. The stadium, you could not get a seat. The noise, the excitement levels, and she just takes it all in her stride. And you could see in Washington what she brings to the court and she plays with such grace.

"There's a certain class about her. I love her attitude. I love the way she goes after the ball. She's a very deceptive tennis player. Being a lefty, she's quite awkward, but that forehand it's not a huge strike, but it does damage."

Croft has likened Eala's serve to that of former Wimbledon champion Angelique Kerber who relied heavily on her left-handed spin, placement, and variation.

She said: "I would imagine that she has built up some kind of locker-room respect right now where you build a certain aura and then that counts for quite a lot on the tour as well because players don't want to face you because of the record that she's building up.

"There's something awkward about a lefty serve, a little bit like Kerber. I remember she didn't have a big serve, but it was so well placed into the court. But also when you put a lot of spin on it and it sometimes has less pace on it, you're forcing your opponents to generate pace and they start to get a bit jittery.

"She keeps notching up the big wins, but she's also backing up the pressure wins.

"She plays under a lot of pressure with all of that excitement from the Filipino community. They turn out in their droves to watch her. That for some people would be a pressure, but she embraces it. She loves it."

Is Eala a US Open contender?

Asked whether Eala could be a contender at the US Open, Croft said: "She's obviously somebody who enjoys being on a big stage. There will be a lot of players that won't want to face her because she's very in form. And I think the hard courts really suit her game."

Eala partnered American tennis legend Venus Williams in the doubles in Toronto this month, resuming their pairing from the Bad Homburg Open in Germany earlier this year.

Williams had high praise for Eala, saying: "Alex is a world star. She's just incredible. Besides the fact of her tennis, she's an incredible person, well spoken, and just an impressive young lady."

Meanwhile, four-time Grand Slam champion Naomi Osaka has thanked Eala for bringing the Filipino community to tennis.

"I think it's great," said the Japanese star. "I finished my match and the little go-kart was taking me back. I looked at the practice court and it was completely full. I was like, 'who's practising right now?' She didn't even go on court yet and then I saw the Filipino flags and I was like, 'um-hum'.

"I think it's awesome. It's so cool that she's building a new community and obviously great for the tournament, because she sells a lot of tickets."

The former British No 1 said: "I've never seen anything like it. The stadium, you could not get a seat. The noise, the excitement levels, and she just takes it all in her stride. And you could see in Washington what she brings to the court and she plays with such grace.

"There's a certain class about her. I love her attitude. I love the way she goes after the ball. She's a very deceptive tennis player. Being a lefty, she's quite awkward, but that forehand it's not a huge strike, but it does damage."

Croft has likened Eala's serve to that of former Wimbledon champion Angelique Kerber who relied heavily on her left-handed spin, placement, and variation.

She said: "I would imagine that she has built up some kind of locker-room respect right now where you build a certain aura and then that counts for quite a lot on the tour as well because players don't want to face you because of the record that she's building up.

"There's something awkward about a lefty serve, a little bit like Kerber. I remember she didn't have a big serve, but it was so well placed into the court. But also when you put a lot of spin on it and it sometimes has less pace on it, you're forcing your opponents to generate pace and they start to get a bit jittery.

"She keeps notching up the big wins, but she's also backing up the pressure wins.

"She plays under a lot of pressure with all of that excitement from the Filipino community. They turn out in their droves to watch her. That for some people would be a pressure, but she embraces it. She loves it."

Is Eala a US Open contender?

Asked whether Eala could be a contender at the US Open, Croft said: "She's obviously somebody who enjoys being on a big stage. There will be a lot of players that won't want to face her because she's very in form. And I think the hard courts really suit her game."

Eala partnered American tennis legend Venus Williams in the doubles in Toronto this month, resuming their pairing from the Bad Homburg Open in Germany earlier this year.

Williams had high praise for Eala, saying: "Alex is a world star. She's just incredible. Besides the fact of her tennis, she's an incredible person, well spoken, and just an impressive young lady."

Meanwhile, four-time Grand Slam champion Naomi Osaka has thanked Eala for bringing the Filipino community to tennis.

"I think it's great," said the Japanese star. "I finished my match and the little go-kart was taking me back. I looked at the practice court and it was completely full. I was like, 'who's practising right now?' She didn't even go on court yet and then I saw the Filipino flags and I was like, 'um-hum'.

"I think it's awesome. It's so cool that she's building a new community and obviously great for the tournament, because she sells a lot of tickets."

articles.summary: El torneo empieza el domingo para ganar un día más de venta de abonos como el Open de Australia y Roland Garros
articles.body: Los tenistas hacía tiempo que reclaman un mayor pastel en el reparto total de beneficios en los torneos del Grand Slam y el US Open ha sido el primero que ha dado un paso adelante para contentar a los profesionales de la raqueta. La dirección del certamen neoyorquino anunció el pasado jueves una cifra récord en premios que asciende a 108 millones de dólares. Eso significa un 20 por ciento más de dinero para los jugadores respecto a la pasada edición. Los campeones individuales, sin ir más lejos, se llevarán a casa un talón de cinco millones y medio de dólares. Carlitos ya ingresó en 2025 el mayor botín de la historia del tenis y que ascendió a cinco millones de dólares, que en euros fueron 4.291.770 euros. Craig Tiley, el dirigente que ha hecho más grande el Open de Australia, desembarca como máximo responsable de la USTA (Federación Americana de Tenis).  El organismo que explota los derechos del último grande del calendario ha puesto unos precios muy elevados para los aficionados que quieran asistir a partir de esta semana a las pistas de Flushing Meadows.  El martes se inicia oficialmente el torneo con el mixto. Una entrada en la Arthur Ashe va desde los 70 dólares hasta los casi 500. Esa misma jornada se celebra un partido de exhibición con Roger Federer como cabeza de cartel. En la central más grande del mundo, con capacidad para más de 23.000 espectadores, se venden los abonos entre 84 dólares y casi 900. Aunque lo más impactante es que para un abono en la primera jornada del cuadro individual, del domingo 30 de agosto -sólo con derecho a las canchas exteriores-, dispara su precio hasta los 323 dólares. Cada día de competición hay sesión de día y de noche, con tickets diferentes en función del horario.  Por el mismo día y el mismo tipo de billete, el Open de Australia cobró a sus seguidores 35 dólares. En Roland Garros la cifra fue de 45 dólares y en Wimbledon, considerado la catedral del tenis, fueron 44 dólares los que tuvieron que desembolsar los aficionados.  Millonarios tendrán que ser los que quieran ver de cerca la final femenina, con abonos de 1.696 dólares. Hasta 2.938 se dispara el ticket más caro para la final masculina.

articles.body:
The second year of the US Open's reformatted mixed doubles is set to kickoff on Tuesday and will feature plenty of top talent.

The event, which is just two days, will offer fans a glimpse at some of the top players before the singles tournament gets underway next week.

Agassi, Serena and more iconic US Open outfits

Click on the post below to see the full bracket.

There's more than just bragging rights at stake: The winning duo will take home a $1 million prize, higher than most prize purses for mixed doubles major tournaments.

The tournament will feature 16 teams competing across two action-packed days.

On Tuesday, both the first round and the quarterfinals will be held, followed by the semifinals and the highly anticipated championship match on Wednesday night.

Matches will follow a best-of-three format, similar to standard doubles events. However, due to the tight schedule, only four games are needed to win a set—except for the championship match, which uses the traditional format.

If a match goes to a third set, a 10-point tie-breaker will determine the winner.

Additionally, no advantage scoring will be used, making each deuce point a thrilling, winner-takes-all moment.

Top seeds Aryna Sabalenka and Novak Djokovic will face Leylah Fernandez and American crowd favorite Frances Tiafoe in a blockbuster first-round matchup.

Fans will also get to see other headliners such as 23-time Grand Slam singles champion Serena Williams teaming up with Carlos Alcaraz.

There are three exciting all-American duos: Amanda Anisimova and Learner Tien, Jessica Pegula and Taylor Fritz, and Emma Navarro and Tommy Paul.

Meanwhile, Gael Monfils and Elina Svitolina will take the court as a husband-wife team.

Sara Errani and Andrea Vassavori will be looking to defend their title, though the exceptionally talented field promises fierce competition.

articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz ha completado este lunes su segundo entrenamiento en las pistas de Flushing Meadows. A diferencia del domingo, donde tuvo su primera toma de contacto en la Louis Armstrong, esta vez ha sido en la Arthur Ashe, la majestuosa central del barrio de Queen's donde ganó la pasada campaña su segundo título.  Alcaraz, que el domingo práctico con su hermano Álvaro y con Samuel López, se ha ejercitado durante una hora al lado de su compatriota Dani Mérida.  Los dos tenistas españoles realizaron un calentamiento de media hora en una de las pistas exteriores y posteriormente se desplazaron a la pista principal. Allí jugaron un set que más bien pareció un partido oficial. El campeón de siete grandes siempre juega pegado a la malla que luce en su brazo derecho desde que regresó a las prácticas en Murcia una vez anunció su renuncia al Masters 1000 de Cincinnati.  La elección de Mérida para la sesión no es casualidad. El madrileño, el 39 del ranking, es uno de los jugadores más en forma del circuito. Sus buenos resultados le han valido para entrar en la convocatoria de España en la serie de Copa Davis ante Chile los días 19 y 20 de septiembre.
